name: City of Winters Seasonal Lifeguard
what_you_do: You watch swimmers and enforce pool rules at the Bobbie Greenwood Community Swim Center. You help open and close the pool, keep it clean and safe, and do water rescues with first aid and CPR when needed.
who_can_apply: 15 or older. You need a lifeguard card (with deep water) and CPR and AED for the Professional Rescuer. You can get them within 30 days after you are hired. First Aid for Public Safety (Title 22) is a plus. You must pass a fingerprint check and a TB skin test. You must be able to work early, late, on holidays and on weekends.
pay_detail: $18.00 to $20.00 per hour (2026 posting), starting at $18. Seasonal, no benefits. The city registers you for and pays for the certification class.
duration: Summer pool season. Exact dates are not on the posting.
deadline_text: Not posted for 2027 yet. Last cycle: the 2026 Lifeguard posting opened Jan 28, 2026 and closed Mar 1, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Expect a new posting around late January 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Answer the extra questions. One asks if you can pass the swim test. You swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes with only your legs and swim 50 yards. Then you bring up a 10 pound object in a timed test. Training is required.
notes: A good choice if you are not certified yet, because the city pays for the certification class. The posting window was short in 2026 (about one month), so check in January. Lifeguards are mandated reporters and must finish that training in the first two weeks. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
